walkthroughs.body_html:
The Early Stuarts & the Origins of the Civil War 1603-1660 — a core area of A-Level History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

The Early Stuarts & the Origins of the Civil War 1603-1660 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with The Early Stuarts & the Origins of the Civil War 1603-1660.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What belief did James I hold about royal authority?
options: The Divine Right of Kings
Parliamentary sovereignty
Republican government
Papal supremacy

mcqs.q: What was the Gunpowder Plot of 1605?
options: A Catholic plot to blow up Parliament
A war with Scotland
A peasant rebellion
A naval invasion

mcqs.q: Which tax extended inland by Charles I caused major resentment?
options: Ship Money
Income tax
Poll tax
Window tax

mcqs.q: What did Charles I do in 1642 to begin the Civil War?
options: Raised his standard at Nottingham
Abdicated the throne
Fled to France
Dissolved the monarchy

mcqs.q: Why did Charles I rule without Parliament from 1629?
options: Parliament abolished itself in 1629.
The Gunpowder Plot started the Civil War.
Frustrated by parliamentary opposition over money and policy, he chose to govern alone, raising revenue by controversial means like Ship Money.
Charles I had no power to call Parliament after 1629.

mcqs.q: Was religion the only cause of the Civil War?
options: The Civil War began because of the Gunpowder Plot.
The Civil War was caused solely by Catholic-Protestant rivalry.
Religion mattered, but disputes over royal power, taxation without consent and trust in Charles I combined to cause the war.
The Gunpowder Plot started the Civil War.

mcqs.q: What did the Gunpowder Plot of 1605 reveal?
options: The Gunpowder Plot started the Civil War.
The Civil War began because of the Gunpowder Plot.
The Gunpowder Plot succeeded in killing the king.
It exposed the desperation of some Catholics under James I and deepened Protestant suspicion of Catholic loyalty.
